chunks: Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah narrated from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When a servant intends to do an evil deed, it is not recorded against him, but if he intends to do a good deed, it is recorded for him.
ai.seo_question: How are good and bad intentions recorded by God before action?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between mere internal intention (himma) and actualized action, establishing that good intentions are rewarded even if unfulfilled, while bad intentions remain unpenalized unless acted upon. This principle underscores the Shia emphasis on the spiritual weight of the heart's disposition, linking directly to the concept of 'amal al-qalbi' (deed of the heart) in jurisprudential and theological discourses. It serves as a foundational text for understanding divine mercy in the accounting of deeds, encouraging believers to cultivate positive intentions as a form of worship in itself.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 8.ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah narrated from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (a) who said,
“When a servant intends to do an evil deed, it is not recorded against him, but if he intends to do a good deed, it is recorded for him.”
